Prufer sequences

Source: R/combinatorics-prufer.R
Prufer.Rd

Prufer(x, n) is SymPy's Prufer: a labeled tree on the nodes 0, ..., n - 1, given either as a list of edges (pairs) or as its Prufer sequence. The fields $prufer_repr, $tree_repr, $nodes, $rank and $size mirror SymPy's. prufer_next() and prufer_prev() move through the trees in rank order, prufer_unrank(rank, n) builds the tree of a rank, prufer_edges(...) turns runs of connected nodes into a list of edges and a node count (relabeled from 0), and prufer_to_prufer() and prufer_to_tree() convert between the two representations.

Usage

Prufer(x, n = NULL)

prufer_next(p, delta = 1)

prufer_prev(p, delta = 1)

prufer_unrank(rank, n)

prufer_to_prufer(tree, n)

prufer_to_tree(prufer)

prufer_edges(...)

Arguments

x

A list of edges or a Prufer sequence.

n

Number of nodes.

p

A Prufer.

delta

Steps to move.

rank

A rank.

tree

A list of edges.

prufer

A Prufer sequence.

...

Runs of nodes (vectors).

Value

A Prufer, a sequence, or a list of edges.

Examples

a <- Prufer(list(c(0, 1), c(0, 2), c(0, 3), c(0, 4)))
a$prufer_repr
#> [1] 0 0 0
a$rank
#> [1] 0
prufer_next(a)$tree_repr
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0 3
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> [1] 1 4
#> 
Prufer(c(1, 1))$tree_repr
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] 1 3
#> 
prufer_edges(c(0, 1, 2, 3), c(1, 4, 5), c(1, 4, 6))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]][[1]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> [[1]][[2]]
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
#> [[1]][[3]]
#> [1] 1 4
#> 
#> [[1]][[4]]
#> [1] 2 3
#> 
#> [[1]][[5]]
#> [1] 4 5
#> 
#> [[1]][[6]]
#> [1] 4 6
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 7
#>
